questions.q: What does this lesson explicitly say about the frameworks it names?
options: This is an orientation to help recognize the names, not legal advice
Every organization is legally required to adopt all three frameworks named
These frameworks are now obsolete and no longer used
They are proprietary and cannot be read by the public
questions.explain: The lesson states directly that it is orientation-level recognition, not legal advice or a compliance manual.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the NIST AI Risk Management Framework?
options: A voluntary U.S. framework organizing AI risk management around functions commonly described as Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage
A binding international law with criminal penalties
A certification exam for data scientists
A specific software product sold by NIST
questions.explain: The lesson describes NIST AI RMF as voluntary guidance built around those four core functions, not a product or binding law.

questions.q: What makes ISO/IEC 42001 distinct from the NIST AI RMF, per the lesson?
options: It is an international standard for an AI management system that organizations can seek formal certification against
It is a tax code specific to AI hardware purchases
It only applies to healthcare organizations
It was published by the United Nations Security Council
questions.explain: ISO/IEC 42001 follows ISO's certifiable management-system pattern, unlike NIST's non-certifiable voluntary guidance.

questions.q: How does the lesson describe the EU AI Act relative to the other two frameworks covered?
options: It is binding law, not voluntary, and classifies AI systems into risk tiers with different obligations
It is entirely voluntary and carries no legal weight
It applies only to AI systems built in the United States
It is identical in structure and enforcement to ISO/IEC 42001
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that the EU AI Act, unlike NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001, is binding law with a risk-tiered structure.

questions.q: What does the lesson recommend doing if a specific framework or regulation actually applies to your organization?
options: Go to that framework's primary source document and involve someone with current legal or compliance expertise
Rely entirely on this single lesson's summary as the final word
Assume the framework hasn't changed since it was first published
Ignore it unless a customer specifically asks about it
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly tells learners to consult the primary source and legal/compliance expertise rather than treat the lesson as definitive.
